title: Change
about: Collocations about change: small and big changes (make a slight alteration, adopt a new approach, kick the habit), everyday phrases with change (change your mind, change the subject, move house) and common traps: become available, problems arise, rise or raise.

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Rise і raise легко сплутати. Rise — без додатка: щось піднімається саме (prices rise, the sun rises). Raise — з додатком: хтось піднімає щось (raise your hand, raise taxes, raise a question). Arise — «виникати» (problems arise), теж без додатка. Найчастіше плутають форми минулого часу, тому вони в таблиці.

rows: The river rose after a week of rain.
The school raised the price of lunches.
A small problem arose at the last minute.

items.pattern: make an adjustment / adjustments (to sth) · make a few / some / minor adjustments · verb: adjust sth
items.meaning: make small changes to something so that it works, fits or suits you better
items.example: I **made a few adjustments** to the car seat, and now my back doesn't hurt on long drives.
more: When the rent went up, we had to **make some adjustments** to our monthly budget.
The optician **made a small adjustment** to my glasses because they kept sliding down my nose.
items.watchOut: «Внести корективи» — make adjustments, не bring adjustments і не introduce corrections. Після adjustment — прийменник to: adjustments to the plan. Можна і дієсловом: I adjusted the seat.

items.pattern: make a slight / small / minor alteration (to sth) · alterations to a plan / a timetable / a dress
items.meaning: change something a little
items.example: We've **made a slight alteration** to the route: we'll stop for lunch in the village, not at the motorway café.
more: The school has **made a slight alteration** to the timetable, so PE is now on Thursdays.
The dentist **made a slight alteration** to my brace, and now it doesn't hurt.
items.watchOut: «Невелика, незначна зміна» — a slight alteration, не a light alteration (light — легкий за вагою або світлий). Вимова: alteration /ˌɔːltəˈreɪʃn/, на початку звук «о», а не «а».

items.pattern: make a modification / modifications (to sth) · make a few / minor / major modifications · verb: modify sth
items.meaning: change parts of something so that it works better or suits a new purpose
items.example: My grandad **made a few modifications** to his bike so he could carry his fishing rods.
more: We had to **make some modifications** to the bathroom when Mum started using a wheelchair.
The recipe is lovely, but I **made one modification**: half the sugar.
items.watchOut: Modification звучить офіційніше, ніж change: у розмові частіше кажуть make a few changes. Дієслово — make: make modifications to the house.

items.pattern: adopt a new / different approach (to sth) · take / try a new approach
items.meaning: start dealing with a problem or situation in a new way
items.example: After months of arguments about homework, we **adopted a new approach**: homework straight after school, then the park.
more: If our first plan doesn't work, we'll **adopt a different approach**.
The hospital has **adopted a new approach** to visiting hours: families can come at any time.
items.watchOut: «Прийняти новий підхід» — adopt або take a new approach, а не accept: accept — погодитися з чужою пропозицією. Не плутай adopt /əˈdɒpt/ (обрати, перейняти; ще — усиновити) з adapt /əˈdæpt/ (пристосувати). Після approach — to: an approach to the problem.

items.pattern: have / get sth altered · have a dress / trousers / a suit altered · structure: have sth done
items.meaning: pay someone, for example a tailor, to change clothes so that they fit better
items.example: My wedding dress was a bit too long, so I **had it altered**.
more: I **had** my old leather jacket **altered**, and it looks like new.
You can **get** the sleeves **altered** at the dry cleaner's on the corner.
items.watchOut: «Віддати перешити» — have / get sth altered: роботу робить хтось інший (have sth done). I altered my dress — я перешила сама. Alter вимовляється /ˈɔːltə/, на початку «о», а не «а».

items.pattern: break a / the habit (of doing sth) · a hard / difficult habit to break · opposite: get into a habit
items.meaning: stop doing something that you have done regularly for a long time
items.example: It took me months to **break the habit** of eating crisps in front of the TV.
more: Biting your nails is a hard **habit to break**.
My dad finally **broke the habit** of leaving his shoes in the middle of the hall.
items.watchOut: «Кинути звичку» — break a habit (нейтрально) або kick the habit (розмовне), не throw a habit. Про паління кажуть give up / quit smoking. Після habit — of + -ing: the habit of eating late.

items.pattern: kick the habit (informal) · usually about smoking, drinking, sugar or coffee
items.meaning: stop doing something harmful that you are addicted to
items.uk: кинути шкідливу звичку, покінчити з нею
items.example: My uncle smoked for thirty years, but he finally **kicked the habit** when his first grandchild was born.
more: I drink far too much coffee. I really need to **kick the habit**.
A friend of mine tried everything to **kick the habit**: patches, gum, even hypnosis.
items.watchOut: Розмовний вираз, майже завжди з the: kick the habit. Зазвичай про залежність — цигарки, алкоголь, солодке, каву. Про звичайні звички частіше кажуть break a habit.

items.pattern: revolutionise the way people do sth · revolutionise sth (travel, farming, medicine)
items.meaning: completely change the way something is done, usually for the better
items.uk: докорінно змінити (те, як…), зробити справжню революцію
items.example: Cheap flights have **revolutionised the way** people go on holiday.
more: The washing machine **revolutionised the way** families spent their Mondays.
Frozen food **revolutionised the way** people shopped and cooked.
items.watchOut: Після the way — одразу підмет і дієслово, без how: the way we travel, а не the way how we travel. Британське написання — revolutionise, американське — revolutionize.

items.pattern: convert to Christianity / Islam / Buddhism / Judaism · a convert (noun) · also: convert sth into sth
items.meaning: change from one religion to another, or start to follow a religion
items.uk: прийняти (іншу) віру, перейти в іншу віру
items.example: After years of reading about it, my uncle **converted to** Buddhism.
more: Many people in the village **converted to** Christianity when the first church was built.
She was brought up without any religion but **converted to** Judaism in her thirties.
items.watchOut: «Прийняти християнство» — convert to Christianity або become a Christian, не accept Christianity. Після convert — прийменник to. Convert sth into sth — переробити, переобладнати: convert the garage into a bedroom. Дієслово — з наголосом на другому складі: /kənˈvɜːt/.

items.pattern: have the power to transform sth / the way we feel · transform sth (into sth)
items.meaning: be able to change something completely, usually in a positive way
items.uk: мати силу (здатність) докорінно змінити, змінити на краще
items.example: The right teacher **has the power to transform** a child's life.
more: A new haircut can really **transform** the way you feel about yourself.
With a few plants and a coat of paint, we **transformed** the dull kitchen.
items.watchOut: «Має силу змінити» — has the power to, не has the force to. Transform — змінити докорінно, часто на краще; не плутай із transfer (перевести, переказати) і translate (перекласти). «Перетворити на» — transform into: transform the attic into a bedroom.

items.pattern: change places / seats (with sb) · swap places · always plural
items.meaning: move to someone else's seat or position while they take yours
items.example: My little sister gets carsick in the back, so we **changed places** and she sat in the front.
more: In the cinema, a very tall man sat in front of my son, so we **changed seats**.
Can we **change places**? The sun's in my eyes.
items.watchOut: Завжди множина: change places / seats (місць два — твоє і чуже), не change the place. «Помінятися з кимось» — change places with sb. Розмовний варіант — swap places.

items.pattern: change jobs / schools / doctors / trains · usually plural
items.meaning: leave one job, school, doctor etc. and go to a different one
items.uk: змінити роботу / перейти в іншу школу / поміняти лікаря
items.example: My brother is fed up with the long hours, so he's going to **change jobs**.
more: My daughter was unhappy at her old school, so we let her **change schools** after Christmas.
We had to **change trains** twice on the way to my grandparents'.
items.watchOut: Зазвичай множина: change jobs, change schools (було одне місце — стане інше). «Змінити роботу» — не change work. Change trains — зробити пересадку.

items.pattern: move house (UK) · move home · or just move · move to a new flat
items.meaning: leave your home and go to live in a different one
items.example: We're **moving house** next month, so the flat is full of boxes.
more: My parents have **moved house** four times since they got married.
**Moving house** with two cats and a baby was a nightmare.
items.watchOut: «Переїжджати» — move house або просто move, не change house (так не кажуть). Про квартиру: we're moving to a new flat.

items.pattern: change your mind (about sth) · compare: make up your mind = decide
items.meaning: decide something different from what you decided or thought before
items.example: I was going to stay in tonight, but I've **changed my mind**. Let's go out.
more: If you **change your mind** about the tickets, just let me know by Friday.
She **changed her mind** three times before she chose the blue paint.
items.watchOut: «Передумати» — change your mind, завжди з присвійним займенником: I've changed my mind, he changed his mind. Не change my opinion (це «змінити погляди») і не change my idea. Make up your mind — інше: «вирішити, зважитися».

items.pattern: change the subject · quickly / hastily change the subject
items.meaning: start talking about something different, often to avoid an awkward topic
items.example: When Gran started asking about my exam results, I quickly **changed the subject**.
more: Can we **change the subject**? All this talk about hospitals is making me nervous.
He's very good at **changing the subject** whenever money comes up.
items.watchOut: «Змінити тему» — change the subject, не change the theme. Theme — тема твору, свята чи вечірки (a party with a pirate theme). Change the topic теж можна, але найчастіше кажуть change the subject.

items.pattern: change the beds / the sheets · strip the beds = take the dirty sheets off
items.meaning: take off the dirty sheets and put clean ones on
items.example: Grandma always **changes the beds** on Sunday mornings.
more: In this hotel they **change the beds** every three days unless you ask.
I've **changed the sheets** on your bed, so it's nice and fresh.
items.watchOut: «Перестелити ліжко» — change the bed / the sheets. Make the bed — інше: просто застелити ліжко (наприклад, уранці). Постільна білизна — bedding або bed linen, не bed underwear.

items.pattern: change the baby · change a nappy (UK) / a diaper (US) · the baby needs changing
items.meaning: take off a baby's dirty nappy and put a clean one on
items.example: Can you **change the baby** while I warm up her milk?
more: My dad had never **changed a nappy** until my little brother was born.
He's wet again. Could you **change** him while I find his pyjamas?
items.watchOut: Підгузок британською — a nappy, американською — a diaper. «Памперс» — назва бренду, англійці так не називають будь-який підгузок. The baby needs changing — малюкові треба поміняти підгузок.

items.pattern: change your clothes · get changed · change (into sth): change into jeans
items.meaning: take off the clothes you're wearing and put on different ones
items.example: I need to **get changed** before dinner. I've been in these clothes since six this morning.
more: He came home from the farm and **changed his clothes** straight away.
Give me five minutes to **change into** something warmer.
items.watchOut: «Переодягнутися» — change, get changed або change your clothes, не change myself і не redress. Clothes /kləʊðz/ — завжди множина; cloth — тканина, cloths — ганчірки.

items.pattern: exchange / change money (into euros, for euros) · the exchange rate · a bureau de change
items.meaning: swap money of one currency for money of another
items.example: Before our trip to Turkey, I **exchanged** two hundred pounds **for** lira.
more: I'll **exchange** my leftover dollars when I get home.
You can **change money** at the post office without paying commission.
items.watchOut: Обміняти гроші — exchange або change money: обидва варіанти природні. «Обмінник» — a bureau de change /ˌbjʊərəʊ də ˈʃɒndʒ/ або a currency exchange, не money change. Курс — the exchange rate, не course.

items.pattern: exchange addresses / phone numbers / details (with sb) · swap numbers (informal)
items.meaning: give each other your address or phone number so you can keep in touch
items.example: At the end of the language course, we all **exchanged addresses** and promised to write.
more: After the bump in the car park, the two drivers **exchanged** names and **addresses**.
We **exchanged phone numbers** at the party, but she never called.
items.watchOut: Не changed addresses — це «змінили адресу», тобто переїхали. «Обмінятися номерами» — exchange numbers або розмовно swap numbers.

items.pattern: exchange ideas / views / opinions (with sb) · share ideas
items.meaning: tell each other what you think about something
items.example: The parents' group meets once a month to **exchange ideas** about healthy packed lunches.
more: It's nice to **exchange views** with other dog owners in the park.
Neighbours met in the church hall to **exchange ideas** for the street party.
items.watchOut: «Обмінятися думками» — exchange ideas / views, не change ideas (це «змінити свої думки»). «Поділитися думками» — share your ideas, не divide.

items.pattern: become available · be / be made available · become available on Monday / from May
items.meaning: start to be possible to get, buy or use
items.uk: з'явитися (у продажу, у доступі), звільнитися, стати доступним
items.example: The flat next door **became available**, so my sister moved in.
more: New dates for the course will **become available** in September.
Please call us if a room **becomes available** for the weekend.
items.watchOut: «З'явитися у продажу, звільнитися» — become available, не get available. Get + прикметник часто означає зміну стану (get tired, get dark), але з available кажуть become або be.

items.pattern: become (very) successful · become a successful writer / businesswoman
items.meaning: start to have success, for example good results, money or fame
items.example: Her little cake shop **became** so **successful** that she opened a second one.
more: Few people **become successful** without years of hard work.
My cousin **became a successful** lawyer, just as everyone expected.
items.watchOut: «Стати успішним» — become successful; get successful звучить неприродно. Get + прикметник — переважно про швидкі, звичні зміни: get tired, get hungry. «Досягти успіху» — succeed або be successful, не reach success.

items.phrase: the standard of living rises / improves
items.pattern: the standard of living / living standards rise / improve / go up · a high / low standard of living
items.meaning: the level of money and comfort that people have gets better
items.example: The **standard of living** in my grandparents' village **has improved** a lot since the new road was built.
more: Most people now have a much higher **standard of living** than their great-grandparents had.
When the mine closed, **living standards** in the town fell.
items.watchOut: «Рівень життя» — standard of living або living standards, не level of life. «Зростає» — rises, improves або goes up; increases і grows з цим виразом зазвичай не вживають.

items.pattern: a big / great / real improvement in sb's performance / health / work
items.meaning: the fact that something gets better
items.example: Since we moved to the coast, there's been a real **improvement in** my son's asthma.
more: Teachers have noticed an **improvement in** Max's handwriting.
There's been a noticeable **improvement in** the service at our local café.
items.watchOut: «Покращення результатів» — an improvement in performance, не an increase in performance. Increase — про кількість (an increase in prices, in traffic). Прийменник — in: an improvement in your English.

items.pattern: problems / difficulties / questions arise · arise – arose – arisen · if any problems arise
items.meaning: problems start to happen
items.example: If any problems **arise** while you're staying in the flat, call the landlord.
more: Questions always **arise** when you start planning a wedding.
Some unexpected costs **arose** during the building work.
items.watchOut: «Виникли проблеми» — problems arose або, розмовно, came up / cropped up; appeared тут зазвичай не кажуть. Не плутай arise – arose – arisen (виникати) з rise – rose – risen (підніматися) і raise – raised (піднімати щось).

items.pattern: sth rises (no object): prices, profits, temperatures, the sun · rise – rose – risen
items.meaning: go up; become higher
items.example: Food prices **rose** sharply last year, so we started growing our own vegetables.
more: The shop's profits **rise** every December.
In June the sun **rises** before five in the morning.
items.watchOut: Rise — без додатка: щось піднімається саме (prices rise). Raise — з додатком: хтось піднімає щось (raise prices). «Ціни ростуть» — prices are rising / going up.

items.pattern: raise your hand / arm · put your hand up (more informal) · raise – raised – raised
items.meaning: lift your hand, for example to ask or answer a question
items.example: **Raise your hand** if you'd like a second helping of pudding.
more: She **raised her hand** to stop the taxi.
At the meeting, only two people **raised their hands** to vote against the plan.
items.watchOut: Підняти руку — raise your hand, не rise your hand: rise не має додатка. У школі часто кажуть put your hand up.

items.pattern: raise taxes / prices / the rent · put up / increase taxes
items.meaning: make taxes, prices or the rent higher
items.example: The new mayor promised not to **raise taxes** for the next two years.
more: Our landlord has **raised the rent** for the third year running.
Shops always **raise** the price of flowers before Valentine's Day.
items.watchOut: Хтось підвищує податки — raise taxes (є додаток). Податки самі зростають — taxes rise / go up. Rise taxes — помилка.

items.pattern: raise a question / an issue / a problem / a point · raise sth at a meeting
items.meaning: mention a question or problem so that people discuss it
items.example: At dinner, Mum **raised the question** of pocket money, and the kids went quiet.
more: I'd like to **raise an issue** about the noise from the flat upstairs.
Your story **raises** an interesting **question**: why didn't anyone call for help?
items.watchOut: «Підняти (порушити) питання» — raise a question / an issue, не rise і не lift a question. Raise a question — винести на обговорення; ask a question — просто запитати.

warmup.uk: Ми обрали новий підхід до кишенькових грошей: тепер діти їх заробляють.
warmup.q: We've ___ a new approach to pocket money: now the kids earn it.
warmup.explain: Обрати новий підхід — adopt (або take) a new approach. Accept — погодитися з чужою пропозицією, adapt — пристосувати.

warmup.uk: Я ніяк не можу позбутися звички спати до обіду на вихідних.
warmup.q: I can't ___ the habit of sleeping until noon at weekends.
warmup.explain: Позбутися звички — break a habit. Throw — калька з «кинути», так не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Ми переїжджаємо, бо нам потрібно більше місця.
warmup.q: We're ___ house because we need more space.
warmup.explain: Переїжджати — move house або просто move. Change house не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Мама одразу змінила тему, коли тато згадав про відпустку.
warmup.q: Mum quickly changed the ___ when Dad mentioned the holiday.
warmup.explain: Змінити тему розмови — change the subject. Theme — тема свята чи твору.
Переодягнутися — get changed або просто change. Change myself — «змінити себе», redress — виправити (несправедливість).

warmup.uk: На весіллі ми з ним обмінялися номерами телефонів.
warmup.q: He and I ___ phone numbers at the wedding.
warmup.explain: Обмінятися — exchange (розмовно swap). Changed numbers — змінили свої номери.

warmup.uk: У країні поступово зростає рівень життя.
warmup.q: The ___ of living in the country is slowly rising.
warmup.explain: Рівень життя — standard of living або living standards, не level of life.

warmup.uk: На зборах вона порушила питання паркування.
warmup.q: At the meeting, she ___ the question of parking.
warmup.explain: Порушити питання — raise a question. Rise не має додатка, lift — підняти щось фізично.

A.q: The chef made a ___ alteration to the recipe: a bit less salt and some fresh herbs.
A.explain: Невелика зміна — a slight alteration. Light — легкий або світлий, thin — тонкий.

A.q: My son's school blazer was far too big, so I ___ it altered.
A.explain: Віддати перешити — have (або get) sth altered: структура have sth done, роботу робить хтось інший.

A.q: Sugar is hard to give up, but my aunt finally ___ the habit.
A.explain: Kick the habit — розмовне «покінчити зі шкідливою звичкою». Throw the habit — калька з «кинути».

B.q: She's bored at the bank and wants to ___ jobs.
B.explain: Змінити роботу — change jobs (множина). Exchange — обмінятися чимось з кимось.

B.q: The baby needs ___. Can you pass me a clean nappy?
B.explain: The baby needs changing — малюкові треба поміняти підгузок.

B.q: My grandparents love to ___ views on politics over breakfast, even though they never agree.
B.explain: Обмінюватися думками — exchange views / ideas. Change — змінювати, divide — ділити на частини.

C.q: A seat ___ available on the earlier train, so we took it.
C.explain: Звільнитися, стати доступним — become available. Get available не кажуть.

C.q: It rained all week, but there's been a big ___ in the weather since Friday.
C.explain: Покращення — an improvement in sth. Increase і growth — про кількість чи розмір.

C.q: Problems ___ on the first day of the camping trip, when the tent started leaking.
C.explain: Виникли проблеми — problems arose (arise – arose – arisen). Raise потребує додатка, rise — підніматися.

M.explain: Температура піднялася сама — rise (rose). Raise потребує додатка: raise the temperature.

M.q: The quiz host asked who knew the answer, and Sam was the first to ___ his hand.
M.explain: Підняти руку — raise your hand. Rise і arise не мають додатка.

M.q: The council has decided to ___ parking charges in the town centre.
M.explain: Підвищити плату чи податки — raise (або put up, increase). Rise — зростати самому, без додатка.

example.title: Gran's new start
example.uk:
Коли помер дідусь, бабусі стало самотньо на фермі, і вона збиралася переїхати. Потім вона передумала й обрала новий підхід: записалася до групи любителів піших прогулянок у селі.

Прогулянки мали силу змінити її настрій на краще, і невдовзі вона покінчила зі звичкою їсти печиво пізно ввечері. Коли в групі звільнилося місце на поїздку до Шотландії, вона одразу його забронювала.

У поїздці вона познайомилася з Тедом, пекарем на пенсії із сусіднього села. Вони обмінялися номерами телефонів, і тепер щосуботи разом ходять на ринок. Звісно, виникли деякі проблеми: Тедів пес ненавидить бабусиного кота. Але коли я питаю, чи це серйозно, бабуся лише всміхається і змінює тему.
example.en:
When Grandad died, Gran felt lonely on the farm and planned to [[move house|b3]]. Then she [[changed her mind|b4]] and [[adopted a new approach|a4]]: she joined a walking group in the village.

The walks [[had the power to transform|a10]] her mood, and soon she [[kicked the habit|a7]] of eating biscuits late at night. When a place [[became available|c1]] on the group's trip to Scotland, she booked it at once.

On the trip she met Ted, a retired baker from the next village. They [[exchanged phone numbers|b10]], and now they go to the market together every Saturday. Of course, a few problems have [[arisen|c5]]: Ted's dog hates Gran's cat. But when I ask if it's serious, Gran just smiles and [[changes the subject|b5]].
